intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib (CDAN1B) is caused by homozygous mutation in the C15ORF41 gene (CDIN1; 615626).

checks.claim: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib (CDAN1B) is caused by homozygous mutation in the C15ORF41 gene (CDIN1).
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous mutations in a predicted endonuclease are a novel cause of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports homozygous C15ORF41 mutations (c.533T>A, p.L178Q in one pedigree; c.281A>G, p.Y94C in two more) in CDAN1 mutation-negative CDA type I families. It presents these as a second cause of CDA I, separate from CDAN1. The 'type Ib' label and the CDIN1 symbol are standard nomenclature that restate the paper's finding.

paragraphs.text: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib (CDAN1B) is a form of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I (CDA I). Most cases of CDA I are caused by mutation in the CDAN1 gene, but no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation is found in about 20% of cases (Babbs et al., 2013). In some of these CDAN1-negative families, CDA I is caused by homozygous mutation in C15ORF41, which encodes a predicted endonuclease (Babbs et al., 2013).

checks.explanation: The C15ORF41-related disorder is described as CDA type I.

paragraphs.text: Sabry et al. (1997) described 3 Bedouin sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I who also had dysmorphic features. These included growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail and phalangeal hypoplasia of the fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of the toes, and hallux valgus. The phenotype varied among the sibs. Sabry et al. (1997) concluded that their report confirmed an association between a subset of CDA I and a specific form of distal limb anomalies, suggesting a distinct entity.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of CDAN1B in the families reported by Babbs et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance: affected individuals, including members of a consanguineous family, carried homozygous mutations in the C15ORF41 gene.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous family of Middle Eastern origin with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type Ib, Babbs et al. (2013) identified a homozygous c.533T-A transversion in the C15ORF41 gene, predicted to result in a leu178-to-gln (L178Q) substitution. The mutation was found by whole genome sequencing and segregation analysis; no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation had been found in this family.
